title: Financial services: Westpac's rolling job cuts near 300 positions as banks swing axe
full_text:
Westpac's job cuts since the start of last month are nearing 300 and are set to keep rising after the bank axed 40 positions last week in its latest round of redundancies.
The nation's oldest bank cut 244 jobs in two tranches last month before telling another 40 staff their jobs no longer existed last week as it restructures its operations to compete with rivals that are also axing roles.
Dubbed Project Catalyst, Westpac's restructure is occurring on advice from consultancy Bain & Co into about 20 different units that bring together staff from different disciplines to deliver banking services such as mortgages or business loans. A source close to the bank confirmed 40 jobs were cut last week and suggested more cuts could follow in months ahead.
While the cuts are nowhere near as severe as the 2500 staff cuts recently announced by NAB or the 3500 job cuts announced by ANZ last year, Westpac's changes point to the pressure on big Australian corporates to trim costs as they spend on digital services.
A Westpac spokesman said the bank had more than 30,000 staff and had hired more than 5000 people in the past year. "While we continue to invest in extra bankers, digital delivery and customer-facing roles, other programs may be completing or require fewer resources," he said in a statement.
"This means from time to time, we make changes that may impact some roles and responsibilities as we actively manage costs and investment. As customer habits change, and the skills and capabilities required in banking continue to evolve, so will our workforce."
He said Westpac offered new jobs to staff who had been redundant when it could, or help to transition to a new career. The Finance Sector Union was contacted for comment.
ANZ, which has a market capitalisation of $120 billion to Westpac's $130 billion, employs about 40,000 people after axing 3500 roles last year. It has also clamped down on staff working from home, this masthead reported last week.
NAB, which has a similar market value to ANZ, announced last month it would remove 2500 jobs. "We will improve productivity, risk outcomes and execution to be a simpler and more efficient bank," chief executive Andrew Irvine said at the time.
Both banks said the job cuts would not be in customer-facing areas. Westpac's restructure also avoids its retail branches.
Australia's big four banks are facing increased competition from Macquarie in the mortgage market, and there are fears AI will make customers more discerning when choosing banking products.
Westpac this month reported a profit of $6.8 billion for the 2026 financial year, down 1 per cent on 2025.
The International Monetary Fund has warned Australia faces the largest increase in unemployment next year among developed countries, albeit from a lower base than many peers.
